node_definition.done_when: Read section 18 of crew-observability-truth and its row in the audit report at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/open-sections-already-landed.html. The section is open. Runs on one backend that end together are classified as one lane event, not as N separate worker failures. Terminal runs on the same backend whose ends fall within a correlation window are grouped, and the group names its likely cause where the stream records one, such as an unknown or unserved model. The live and recovery classification in reckon/crew/recovery.py carries the grouping, and the fleet surfaces in reckon/crew/query.py report it once rather than once per run. A single terminal run, and terminals on different backends, are never grouped. tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py builds live pointers in a temporary config home: three runs on one backend ending within the window, one on another backend, and one on the first backend ending well outside the window. It asserts exactly one lane event naming the three, with the other two left as individual terminals. It fails at your base. Existing recovery and query tests keep passing; grep tests/ for the classification entry points and query surfaces to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/simultaneous-ends-are-one-lane-event.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
